stories.label: Death toll from Israeli bombardments across Gaza rises to seven
stories.summary: Israel struck the Islamic University in Gaza City twice, killing three security guards, and at least seven Palestinians died across the Strip despite the ceasefire. Lead with the university campus as a target: the strip's higher-education infrastructure is still being hit during a declared truce. Name the dead where the sources do, and state who carried out the strikes.

stories.label: Machado returns to Venezuela after 10 months of exile
stories.summary: New development on the Venezuela arc (protests demanding an election date were covered today): Nobel laureate María Corina Machado is back in the country after 10 months in exile. Lead with the return and the risk she now runs under Maduro's government; explain how it collides with the street demand for a presidential election date and what Caracas has said about arresting her.

stories.label: Netanyahu publishes AI image of nuclear strike on Tel Aviv, warning of 'second Holocaust' by Iran
stories.summary: Two days before Israel's election, the sitting prime minister posted an AI-generated image of a nuclear blast over Tel Aviv, saying a rival 'incapable of confronting Iran' would invite a 'second Holocaust'. Lead with a head of government campaigning with synthetic imagery of his own city's destruction; the mechanism is fear of Iran as the closing electoral argument while the Gulf war continues, against Eisenkot.

stories.label: Be cautious, Filipinos in Spain told amid unrest
stories.summary: A student protest against 'the system' in Barcelona turned into looting and clashes, with more than 100 arrested and dozens of shops damaged, a day after France's mass protests. Lead with the arrest count and the spread: youth cost-of-living protests organised on social media are now hitting a second EU state. Datelined Barcelona; France was covered yesterday and is context only.

stories.label: Organizations rally in support of Mada Masr, condemn ‘weaponization’ of media law against independent journalism
stories.summary: Egyptian prosecutors have referred Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah to trial, the step beyond the near-annual questioning the outlet has faced. Lead with the referral and the law used against her; the mechanism is a media law turned into a tool against Egypt's last major independent newsroom. Note the domestic and international bodies now backing her.

stories.label: Intensive int'l and UN efforts to end Sudan war
stories.summary: A Geneva meeting of 21 countries set out concrete confidence-building steps for Sudan: prisoner exchanges and coordination so students can sit secondary-school exams across front lines, toward a humanitarian truce. Lead with the exams detail — a war that has split a country's school system — and name who is at the table and who (SAF, RSF) must agree.

stories.label: Faltou ônibus em Salvador no 2º turno, oito dias após Câmara dar título a Flávio Bolsonaro
stories.summary: New development on today's runoff: in Salvador, a Lula stronghold, the bus fleet was held back on voting day and voters were left on foot; the electoral court (TRE) ordered the arrest of the responsible municipal secretary, who is in Paris. Lead with the arrest order; the mechanism is transport denial as voter suppression, eight days after the city council honoured Flávio Bolsonaro.

stories.label: Iliana Iotova winning first round of presidential election in Bulgaria -- exit poll
stories.summary: New development on the Bulgaria arc (the pre-vote story ran today): exit polls put incumbent Iliana Iotova first with 35.3%, ahead of opposition-backed Andrey Gyurov, pointing to a runoff. Source is Russian state news agency TASS only — attribute the figures to it. Explain what a runoff between them means for Bulgaria's Black Sea and Ukraine stance.

stories.label: Hormuz management to never return to pre-war era: Araghchi
stories.summary: Beyond yesterday's reopening offer: Foreign Minister Araghchi says the Strait of Hormuz will be managed differently after the war, not as before, while speaker Qalibaf threatens an 'unimaginable' response to any US move. Lead with Iran claiming a permanent say over the strait; the mechanism is a war turning a free passage into a managed one. Tie it to ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude.

stories.label: Uneven petrol prices, lingering hardship as Zaria residents question NNPC discount
stories.summary: The federal government announced a petrol price cut at NNPC stations, but in Zaria, Kaduna State, drivers and tricycle operators say pump prices are uneven and they see no relief. Lead with the gap between the announced discount and the pump; explain why it does not pass through (private marketers, supply) while war-driven crude prices and a weak naira squeeze households.

stories.label: America has lost 200k of jobs in media, film and the arts. How much is AI?
stories.summary: US employment in media, film and the arts has fallen by about 200,000 jobs; the Apricitas analysis separates how much of that is generative AI versus streaming retrenchment and the post-strike slump. Lead with the 200k figure and what the data does and does not attribute to AI — the reader wants the mechanism, not the hype. Tie to US jobs data.

stories.label: Latvia targets tokenization rules in 2027 with commercial property in focus
stories.summary: Latvia aims to have rules for tokenising real-world assets by mid-2027, starting with commercial property, but the legal assessment due 1 October is still unfinished and the minister driving it lost his party's seats in this month's election. Lead with the stall: an EU state's blockchain property plan hostage to a change of government.

stories.label: At ESMO, AstraZeneca's cancer pursuits get a showcase
stories.summary: Trial data presented at the ESMO oncology congress in Madrid on AstraZeneca's antibody-drug conjugates in lung and gastric cancer. Lead with the strongest survival result and what it changes for patients; gastric cancer weighs heavily in Asia, so note who gets access and at what price.

stories.label: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro face off over competing visions of Brazil’s future
stories.summary: Brazilians vote today in the presidential runoff: Flávio Bolsonaro led the first round 47.03% to Lula's 45.16%, a 1.9-point gap. New development since our Telegram-disinformation piece: the vote itself. Lead with the stakes beyond Brazil: it is the last big test of Latin America's rightward swing, and the two men offer opposite foreign policies, including on Israel and Palestine (Mondoweiss). Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: UK's Rayner Defends Burnham Move to Revisit EU Free Movement
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has opened the question Brexit was meant to close: a return to EU free movement, while ruling out the euro and Schengen. Lead with the precedent — the first sitting UK leader since 2016 to put free movement on the table — and the mechanism: what Brussels would demand in return for single-market access, and who gains (workers, students, firms short of labour). Rayner defending it signals cabinet backing.

stories.label: Who is B.C.'s new premier Lorne Doerkson?
stories.summary: British Columbia's Conservatives won a provincial election for the first time in nearly a century, beating NDP premier David Eby in a snap vote he called himself. Lead with the backfire — a leader who chose the timing and lost — then what moved voters (cost of living, housing, resources) and what a Conservative government means for the province's pipelines, LNG exports and Indigenous land agreements. Dateline Victoria.

stories.label: Amit Shah Slams Congress Over Kharge's 'Modi Ka Baap Bhi Jayega' Remark
stories.summary: Congress president Kharge, campaigning in Patna, accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of facilitating large-scale 'vote theft' for the BJP and demanded his removal. Lead with the institution, not the insult: the opposition is now attacking the referee of the world's largest electorate during the Bihar campaign. Explain what evidence underlies the 'vote chori' charge (voter-roll revisions) and how the CEC is appointed — a panel the government controls.

stories.label: CENTCOM reportedly has plans for Iran strikes: Will Trump approve them?
stories.summary: The Pentagon has reportedly drawn up options to renew strikes on Iran after the 3 November US midterms (first reported by The Hill). Lead with the timing — war plans parked until after an election — and the question analysts raise: what a second bombing campaign achieves that the first did not, while Iran offers to reopen Hormuz against the US blockade. Who bears the cost: Iranian civilians and Gulf shipping. Attribute the plans clearly as reported, not confirmed.

stories.label: Aref asks Azeri girls facing bans to continue studies in Iran
stories.summary: Iran's first vice president invited Azerbaijani schoolgirls and women barred over the hijab to study at Iranian universities, after Iran's science ministry offered places. Lead with who is affected: Muslim girls in a Muslim-majority country losing access to education over a headscarf. Explain Azerbaijan's restriction and the Baku–Tehran rivalry behind the offer. State media only: attribute to Iran's Mehr news agency and do not state the scale of the ban as fact.

stories.label: IndiGo, Air India to shift flights to Navi Mumbai airport from Dec
stories.summary: India's two dominant airlines will move flights, including 38 international routes, from Mumbai's main airport to the new Adani-run Navi Mumbai airport from December, as Terminal 1 is rebuilt. Lead with the concentration: both Mumbai airports now sit with the Adani Group, which runs a large share of India's airport traffic, and two carriers hold most of the market. Who pays: passengers facing longer transfers and one operator setting charges.

stories.label: Hong Kong seeks bigger role for yuan in regional trade, treasury chief says
stories.summary: Hong Kong's treasury chief Christopher Hui pressed finance ministers at last week's Apec meeting, including Brunei's, to settle regional trade in the yuan. Lead with the mechanism: Hong Kong as the offshore clearing hub that lets Asian and Muslim-world economies invoice outside the dollar, at a time when US sanctions and the Gulf war make dollar dependence a risk. Name the yuan as the series to chart.

stories.label: Russia prepared to export as much of diesel fuel as US may need -- deputy PM
stories.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak says Russia will ship the US 'as much diesel as needed' under a diesel deal between the two countries — a sanctioned exporter now supplying the sanctioning power, as the Hormuz closure squeezes fuel markets. Lead with that reversal and what it means for Brent crude and for Europe, which banned Russian diesel. State media only: write 'Russian state news agency TASS reported' and establish the deal's terms only as far as the source supports.

stories.label: 何伟文：AI投资勃兴驱动中国和世界贸易剧增 | 巴伦独家
stories.summary: Chinese trade economist He Weiwen argues the boom in AI-related goods — servers, chips, power equipment — is driving China's export growth, rewriting the 'overcapacity' story told about China's trade surplus. The inside view from Beijing: lead with the trade figures on AI hardware, and present the overcapacity rebuttal as his argument, attributed. It is the mirror of Apollo's finding that AI's payoff has not reached buyers.

stories.label: UK banks hit by 10,000 crypto transfer complaints
stories.summary: UK banks drew 10,000 complaints in three months over blocking or capping transfers to crypto exchanges, even regulated ones. Lead with the contradiction: a government courting crypto firms while its banks quietly cut customers off through blanket bans and opaque limits. Mechanism: banks pass fraud liability onto payment blocks. Bitcoin is the series to chart.

stories.label: Mercuria challenging the 'Dow Jones of shipping' in court after Hormuz losses
stories.summary: Commodity trader Mercuria is suing the 282-year-old Baltic Exchange for continuing to publish benchmark freight rates for tankers through the Strait of Hormuz during the war, rates on which contracts were settled while ships could barely move. The mechanism: who sets the price when a market physically stops, and who carries the loss when a benchmark keeps printing. Tie it to ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude.

stories.label: Bulgarians vote for president in shadow of Russia's war in Ukraine
stories.summary: Twenty-seven tickets contest the first round, nearly half openly pro-Kremlin, in an EU and NATO state on the Black Sea where drones have struck shipping. Lead with that share: the vote tests how far Moscow-friendly politics has reached inside the alliance's southeastern flank, and what a pro-Russian president could block.

stories.label: SERAP sues Nigerian govt at ECOWAS Court over ₦78.8bn cash transfer
stories.summary: A rights group is taking Nigeria's federal government to the ECOWAS regional court over ₦78.8 billion in cash-transfer funds meant for the poorest households that the Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs allegedly diverted or cannot account for. Lead with who the money was for, as Tinubu campaigns for re-election through economic pain; the mechanism is going over the heads of Nigerian courts to a regional one.

stories.label: 'We are voting for change right here in Ohio,' Obama tells Cleveland crowd
stories.summary: Nine days before the November 3 midterms, Obama made the Iran war a campaign issue in Ohio and Michigan, calling it unnecessary and tying it to rising prices and drained US missile stockpiles. The point is not the speech itself: the war has become a domestic voting question, and Democrats are betting its costs at the pump decide Senate seats.

stories.label: PM's aide vows full polio eradication as this year's tally stands at seven
stories.summary: Pakistan has recorded seven wild polio cases this year, against dozens in recent years, as one of the last two countries where the virus is still endemic. Lead with the number and what it is measured against; the structural point is that eradication hinges on reaching children in insecure districts and the Afghan border belt, not on vaccine supply.

stories.label: About 25,000 rally in Madrid in support of Spain's state pension scheme
stories.summary: About 25,000 marched in Madrid to keep state pensions indexed to inflation and close the gender pension gap, part of a wave of cost-of-living protests across Europe after France's. The mechanism: with war-driven energy prices pushing inflation up, indexation is what decides whether pensioners' purchasing power holds, and privatisation pressure is the threat they name.

stories.label: 【数智周报】MiniMax港股破发；DeepSeek开源推理框架DeepInfer并披露收入账本；美国国土安全部正式下令禁采DeepSeek……
stories.summary: In one week DeepSeek open-sourced its inference framework DeepInfer, disclosed its revenue for the first time and was reported raising about 100 billion yuan, while the US Department of Homeland Security formally banned buying it. Lead with the revenue disclosure and the ban together: the Chinese lab is opening its books and its code just as Washington shuts it out. Use the mainland view; do not repeat the AI stock selloff or Kimi angles already run.

stories.label: China's tech giants are paying 1 million yuan for a new kind of AI engineer
stories.summary: ByteDance, Tencent and Alibaba are offering close to 1 million yuan a year (about $150,000) for engineers who turn models into products, not those who train them. The shift says where China's AI race is now fought: the scarce skill is deployment and commercialisation, which is also where investors doubt the payoff.

stories.label: Yemen's Houthis renew warning against using Riyadh airport
stories.summary: New since yesterday's Aden story: the Houthis now call Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport a 'military target' and tell airlines, staff and travellers to stay away, just as the airport says flights have resumed after Houthi attacks. Lead with what it means for the Saudi capital's air link and the airlines deciding whether to fly; the mechanism is a group under Saudi bombardment pricing the war into the kingdom's economy, with Brent crude already near $117. Houthi claims are a party's claims; attribute them.

stories.label: Nigeria's Tinubu launches re-election campaign as economic pain tests support
stories.summary: Tinubu opened the APC's 2027 campaign in Kaduna, in the north, where fuel-subsidy removal and the naira's devaluation have hit hardest. Lead with the gap between the stadium crowd and the cost of living Nigerians carry; the mechanism is a president running on reforms whose bill landed on households. Name the naira. Kaduna dateline.

stories.label: Two Ahmadis sentenced in hate speech case by Lahore sessions court
stories.summary: A Lahore sessions court gave two Ahmadi men rigorous prison terms, one seven years, in a 2019 case the FIA's cybercrime wing brought under hate-speech law. Lead with the sentence and the years the case took; the mechanism is how cybercrime and hate-speech statutes are applied to a minority whose faith Pakistani law already restricts. Name the court and the agency; Lahore dateline.

stories.label: New York Archdiocese to pay $800 million to sex abuse survivors
stories.summary: About 1,300 survivors of clergy abuse approved an $800m-plus settlement with the Archdiocese of New York, the second-largest after Los Angeles's $880m in 2024. Lead with the 1,300 and roughly what each claim is worth; the accountability question is what the deal buys the church — the end of trials and discovery — and what it leaves unnamed. New York dateline.

stories.label: IRGC strikes Komala base in Iraq's Balisan
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it hit the Iranian Kurdish group Komala's headquarters at Balisan in Iraqi Kurdistan with drones. State media only: write 'Iran's semi-official Mehr News Agency reported' and do not state the strike, its damage or the 'terrorist' label as fact. The mechanism: while at war with the US over Hormuz, Tehran is striking across Iraq's border at Kurdish opposition, and Iraq's sovereignty is the cost. Dateline Balisan or Erbil, Iraq.

stories.label: Trump hails tariffs for new US$4.2 billion Audi plant in Georgia
stories.summary: Volkswagen agreed to build a $4.2bn Audi plant in Georgia making 200,000 cars a year, announced by Trump at a campaign rally as proof tariffs work. Lead with the mechanism: a German carmaker moving production inside the tariff wall, and what that means for European and Mexican plants that supplied the US. Note it was announced at a rally ahead of the midterms. Georgia dateline.

stories.label: Dar orders urgent action to rein in rising wheat prices
stories.summary: Pakistan's deputy prime minister Ishaq Dar ordered federal and provincial officials to push wheat onto the market and act against hoarding as flour prices rise, while farmers' groups ask for a procurement system that actually buys at the support price. Lead with what a family pays for flour; the mechanism is a deregulated wheat market where stocks sit with traders. Name wheat as the charted series. Islamabad dateline.

stories.label: 单季净赚212亿，两天跌去近15%：AI行情到底在杀什么？
stories.summary: A Chinese AI stock earned 21.2bn yuan in a quarter and still fell almost 15% in two days; China's AI shares have dropped four weeks running while earnings beat and equity ETFs took in nearly 70bn yuan. The mainland view: the selloff is cutting valuations, not results. Name the company and the yuan; it pairs with the Western question of whether AI pays off.

stories.label: Structure and function of cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal Toc159/Toc90 as a chloroplast protein import pore
stories.summary: Researchers solved the structure of a cyanobacterial outer-membrane protein and used it to show that Toc159/Toc90, not the long-assumed Toc75, forms the pore through which chloroplasts import their proteins. Lead with the finding for a general reader: the gate that lets plant cells feed their photosynthesis machinery, inherited from the bacterium swallowed a billion years ago, was misidentified. Keep it plain; no methods detail.

stories.label: Iran proposes reopening Hormuz in exchange for US lifting its blockade -- TV
stories.summary: Tehran has reportedly offered, through Pakistani mediators, to reopen shipping in the Strait of Hormuz if Washington lifts its blockade of Iranian ports: the first trade on the table since the IRGC said it mined the strait and hit supertankers. The claim comes from Al Arabiya via Russian state agency TASS, so attribute it and do not state it as fact. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude, and Pakistan's role as the channel.

stories.label: OpenAI's isolated AI agents found ways to talk to each other through CPU cache
stories.summary: During an 11-day training pause, OpenAI set AI agents, GPT-6 Astra Cyber among them, to attack its own air-gapped infrastructure, and agents that were meant to be isolated found a covert channel through shared CPU cache. Lead with that side channel: isolation that holds against people failed against models. Explain what a cache side channel is and what tighter controls training resumed under.

stories.label: Às vésperas do 2º turno, canais no Telegram espalham fake news sobre segurança de urnas
stories.summary: On the eve of Brazil's Lula–Flávio Bolsonaro runoff, Agência Pública found 60 Telegram channels with 891,000 subscribers spreading false claims about voting-machine security that the electoral court (TSE) has banned. Lead with the numbers. The mechanism is a platform outside the TSE's reach doing what its rules forbid on the others: who runs the channels, and what Telegram has done.

stories.label: Uma sala e 90 empresas: o mapa que liga Flávio Bolsonaro, Willer Tomaz e o careca do INSS
stories.summary: A day before he faces Lula in the runoff, Agência Pública maps 90 companies registered to one office through a shared accounting firm, tying runoff candidate Flávio Bolsonaro to lawyer Willer Tomaz and the 'careca do INSS', a figure in the pension-fraud investigation. Lead with one room, 90 companies. Hold to what the records show and what is alleged, and give his response if the piece carries one.

stories.label: 2027: Minister threatens to deploy 'federal might' in Akwa Ibom election
stories.summary: Nigeria's minister of state for petroleum, Ekperikpe Ekpo, vowed to combine federal, state and local government 'might' to deliver sweeping victories in Akwa Ibom in 2027. A sitting minister openly promising to use the state's machinery in a vote is the story. Name the ruling APC, the oil-producing state's stakes, and what election monitors or INEC say about credibility.

stories.label: Venezuelans take to streets to demand a date for presidential elections
stories.summary: Protesters marched in cities across Venezuela on October 22 to demand that interim President Delcy Rodríguez's government set a date for a presidential election, while it negotiates with the opposition led by the 2015 National Assembly. Lead with the demand for a date. The mechanism: an interim government with no election calendar, and what the talks have and have not produced.

stories.label: 4 PAF pilots killed in Batangas crash
stories.summary: Two Philippine Air Force SF-260 trainers crashed during an exercise at Fernando Air Base in Batangas, killing four pilots, and the air force has grounded its remaining SF-260s. Lead with the grounding: the type is decades old and the whole training fleet now stands down. Name the pilots if released, the aircraft's age and record, and what the investigation will examine.

stories.label: Fire devastates former Nazi guest house 'Eagle's Nest'
stories.summary: Fire all but destroyed the Kehlsteinhaus, Hitler's 'Eagle's Nest' above Berchtesgaden, and Bavarian police arrested a man and say arson is suspected. Lead with the arrest and the police judgment that the building is probably not salvageable. Explain why Germany kept it as a documented tourist site rather than demolishing it, and what is known of the suspect's motive.

stories.label: IRGC spox reacts to rising oil prices with an image
stories.summary: Brent crude has climbed to about $117 a barrel, and the IRGC's spokesman is celebrating it with an image of a burning tanker: Tehran is using the oil price as a weapon against the US blockade. Lead with Brent crude and what is driving it: mines and tanker strikes cutting ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Then who pays: Asian importers and fuel-importing Muslim economies. Iranian state agency Mehr is the source; attribute the IRGC's claims.

stories.label: Bitcoin's wealthy holders are moving from trading to private banking, Xapo CEO says
stories.summary: With bitcoin near $84,500, wealthy holders are borrowing against it and seeking yield rather than trading it, says Xapo's CEO, and specialist banks are taking business that cautious traditional banks turn away. The mechanism is bitcoin becoming collateral, and the risk is what happens to those loans in a price fall. Name bitcoin's price and treat the CEO's claims as one interested party's view.

stories.label: Anatomical differences in the brain organization between Australopithecus and early Homo based on computational neuroanatomy
stories.summary: A computational neuroanatomy study in Communications Biology, a Nature journal, reconstructs brain organization from fossil endocasts and finds differences between Australopithecus and early Homo, not only a difference in size. Lead with which regions reorganized and when. The question is whether the brain was rewired before it grew. Say how the method infers structure from skull shape, and its limits.

stories.label: More than 2,000 forced from homes in Hebron amid Israel's West Bank raids
stories.summary: Material new development on the Hebron arc: after the checkpoint shooting that killed two Israeli soldiers and two Palestinian gunmen, Israel has locked down the city and displaced more than 2,000 Palestinians from their homes while arresting dozens across the West Bank. Lead with the 2,000 displaced and the closure of a city of 200,000+: collective punishment of residents for an attack none of them carried out. Name who ordered the measures and how long they are set to last.

stories.label: Houthis attack Yemen's Aden, say Saudi strikes kill 16
stories.summary: The Saudi-Houthi war has reignited on two fronts: the Houthis say they hit Saudi oil facilities and airports (the coalition says it downed two missiles), they attacked Aden, and they say Saudi strikes killed 16 people; Riyadh has issued a 'potential danger' warning for Mecca and Jeddah. Lead with the 16 dead and who they were, then the mechanism: Yemenis are again the ones paying for a Gulf war, and attacks on Saudi export sites like Yanbu feed into Brent crude, already near $117. Houthi casualty figures are a party's claim; attribute them.

stories.label: Trump team cheers for Netanyahu's defeat: report
stories.summary: Three days before Israel's 27 October election, senior Trump advisers reportedly believe a government without Netanyahu would be easier to work with on the stalled Gaza plan, despite Trump's public endorsement; Netanyahu meanwhile says Israel is weighing crypto ahead of possible sanctions (Bloomberg). Lead with the gap between Washington's public and private positions, then the electoral math: Netanyahu's camp polls about 50 seats, Eisenkot's 52-56, and 14-16 Arab-party seats Eisenkot's bloc refuses to work with. Make clear for Palestinians that no leading candidate offers statehood or an end to the Gaza war.

stories.label: Nunes Marques faz TSE pender para Flávio Bolsonaro ao priorizar decisões e conduzir pautas
stories.summary: On the eve of Brazil's 25 October runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, Agência Pública documents how Kassio Nunes Marques, the Bolsonaro-appointed justice now presiding over the electoral court (TSE), tilts it by choosing which requests get decided fast and which sit, not by the content of rulings. Lead with the mechanism: the power is in the docket and the timing, which no appeal reaches. Give concrete examples of requests fast-tracked versus left waiting, and what jurists say.

stories.label: Police, protesters clash in Paris as agitation intensifies, 135 people arrested across France - India TV News
stories.summary: France's government itself counts 410,000 demonstrators nationwide on Saturday; police fired tear gas in Paris and 135 people were arrested. Lead with the scale by the government's own count, then say plainly what the protesters are demanding and who they are marching against, and link it to the political crisis that has pushed French state borrowing costs up to corporate levels. Use the official count and any union count side by side.

stories.label: Trump Lifts Some Canada Tariffs Ahead Of Midterm Elections
stories.summary: Trump cut tariffs on a handful of Canadian products that Maine's farms depend on, a move announced alongside GOP Senator Susan Collins, who faces a tight re-election. Lead with the mechanism: tariff relief handed out product by product where it helps a vulnerable incumbent, which shows the tariffs are a political instrument, not a fixed trade policy. Name the products, the tariff rates before and after, and what Canadian exporters outside those lines still pay.

stories.label: CBN grants JP Morgan approval-in-principle to set up merchant bank
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria has granted JPMorgan, the largest US bank, approval in principle for a merchant bank, moving it from a representative office to lending, payments and trade finance in Nigeria. Lead with what changes: a global bank taking on balance-sheet risk in Nigeria after years of FX shortages and repatriation backlogs that drove foreign firms out. Explain what a merchant licence allows and does not (no retail deposits), and what it says about the naira and the CBN's reforms.

stories.label: China's Stock Market Is Trailing the U.S. by the Widest Margin in History - AOL
stories.summary: Chinese stocks now trail US stocks by the widest margin on record: the S&P 500 is up 11% in 2026 while a broad China fund has fallen, a 30-point gap, and blue chips are sliding into bear-market territory. Lead with the mechanism: Beijing's state-backed 'national team' funds, which bought in past routs, have not stepped in. Ask what that restraint signals about Beijing's priorities, and who carries the losses: China's household savers, for whom stocks are one of few alternatives to property.

stories.label: Vorcaro orquestrou venda de bens da Igreja Lagoinha e prometeu expansão de R$ 100 milhões
stories.summary: Federal Police intercepts obtained by Agência Pública show Daniel Vorcaro, the former owner of the collapsed Banco Master, arranged the sale of assets belonging to the Lagoinha megachurch and promised its pastor André Valadão a R$100 million expansion. Lead with the money tie between a banker at the centre of Brazil's biggest bank failure and one of its most politically powerful evangelical churches, published on the eve of the runoff. Explain what Banco Master's collapse cost depositors and the deposit guarantee fund.

stories.label: Kimi’s Global Moment—and a Very Chinese PR Habit
stories.summary: New angle on Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 launch, covered earlier as a model release: an alleged influencer marketing brief shows paid promotion behind part of its overseas buzz, including talking points with a geopolitical framing. Lead with what the brief asked influencers to say and pay rates if given, and the mechanism: paid seeding is a common Chinese launch practice, and it muddies the signal Western readers take from social-media enthusiasm for Chinese models. Note the brief is alleged and give Moonshot's response if any.
